own_solution.law: Energy conservation gives mv²/2 = GMm/R. With M = (4π/3)ρR³, comparison with Earth gives v = ve(R/RE)sqrt(ρ/ρE) = 11.19(3390/6371)sqrt(3.93/5.51) = 5.02855 km/s. A same-density planetary coating replaces R with R + q.
assumptions: The probe travels ballistically after launch.
The probe's mass is negligible compared with the planet's mass.
After a planetary coating is added, launch occurs from the new outer surface.
The stated spherical, nonrotating, atmosphere-free model applies, with other bodies' gravity ignored.

notes: All certified answers agree with energy conservation: planetary radius increments of 120, 310 and 470 km give 5.20655, 5.48839 and 5.72572 km/s, respectively. Probe mass cancels, and the moon and earlier simulation have no influence under the stated model.
